notes:
I couldn't do any research for Psalm 128, so I haven't written any notes. My one attempt to fetch the pages failed with the error "no more code_execution tool calls remaining this turn," and nothing loaded. That includes Enduring Word, Gill, Ellicott, the Pulpit Commentary, Matthew Henry, Precept Austin, the NET Bible notes and Augustine on New Advent.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and to give a URL for every point. Writing notes from memory would break both rules, so I've left them out.

If you ask again in a new turn, I'll start with these pages:

- **Traditional reading:** enduringword.com/bible-commentary/psalm-128/, plus the Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit and Matthew Henry pages for Psalm 128 on biblehub.com, Spurgeon's *Treasury of David* (on spurgeon.org or studylight.org), and preceptaustin.org.
- **Protestant differences:** Wesley's notes (wesley.nnu.edu), Ligonier, Desiring God, GTY and LCMS/1517, especially on verses 1–4 and how the blessings promised to those who fear the Lord should be read.
- **Other views:** netbible.org notes on the Hebrew of verses 2 and 5, and bibleodyssey.org on the "songs of ascents." For Catholic and Orthodox readings, Augustine's exposition on New Advent (listed as Psalm 127 there, because of the older numbering), catholic.com and oca.org. For prosperity teaching, gotquestions.org and similar pages on verses 2 and 4.
